/*
    Silver: delivered orders only, with every SLA timestamp guaranteed non-null.
    Feature engineering is deliberately kept out of this model; it belongs to
    int_order_sla_calculated.
*/

with source as (

    select *
    from {{ source('bronze', 'raw_orders') }}

    select
        trim(order_id)                                              as order_id,
        trim(customer_id)                                           as customer_id,
        lowerUTF8(trim(order_status))                               as order_status,
        toDateTime(assumeNotNull(order_purchase_timestamp))         as order_purchase_timestamp,
        toDateTime(assumeNotNull(order_approved_at))                as order_approved_at,
        toDateTime(assumeNotNull(order_delivered_carrier_date))     as order_delivered_carrier_date,

      and order_purchase_timestamp is not null
      and order_approved_at is not null
      and order_delivered_carrier_date is not null
      and order_delivered_customer_date is not null
      and order_estimated_delivery_date is not null

)

from cleaned
order by order_purchase_timestamp desc
limit 1 by order_id

/*
    Silver: order line items with a deterministic composite key and
    non-negative financial measures.
*/

with source as (

    select *
    from {{ source('bronze', 'raw_order_items') }}

),

cleaned as (

    select
        trim(order_id)                                  as order_id,
        toUInt16(order_item_id)                         as order_item_id,
        concat(trim(order_id), '-', toString(order_item_id)) as order_item_sk,
        trim(product_id)                                as product_id,
        trim(seller_id)                                 as seller_id,
        toDateTime(shipping_limit_date)                 as shipping_limit_date,
        coalesce(price, 0)                              as price,
        coalesce(freight_value, 0)                      as freight_value
    from source
    where notEmpty(trim(order_id))
      and notEmpty(trim(product_id))
      and notEmpty(trim(seller_id))
      and coalesce(price, 0) >= 0
      and coalesce(freight_value, 0) >= 0

)

from cleaned
order by order_item_id
limit 1 by order_item_sk

/*
    Gold dimension: one row per customer_id with delivery location, purchase
    history, and a simple frequency segment. One customer_id represents one
    order in the Olist schema; customer_unique_id links repeat buyers.
*/

with customer_metrics as (

    select
        customer_id,
        count()                                             as total_orders,
        countIf(is_delayed = 1)                             as delayed_orders,
        round(countIf(is_delayed = 1) * 100.0 / count(), 2) as delay_rate_pct,
        round(avg(actual_delivery_days), 2)                 as avg_delivery_days,
        round(avg(review_score), 2)                         as avg_review_score,
        round(sum(total_order_value), 2)                    as total_spend,
        min(order_purchase_timestamp)                       as first_order_at,
        max(order_purchase_timestamp)                       as last_order_at
    from {{ ref('fct_operational_delivery') }}
    group by customer_id

),

customer_attributes as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_customers') }}

),

geolocation as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_geolocation') }}

)

select
    m.customer_id                               as customer_id,
    coalesce(c.customer_unique_id, '')          as customer_unique_id,
    coalesce(c.customer_city, 'unknown')        as customer_city,
    coalesce(c.customer_state, 'unknown')       as customer_state,
    coalesce(c.customer_zip_code_prefix, '')    as customer_zip_code_prefix,
    g.lat                                       as customer_lat,
    g.lng                                       as customer_lng,

    m.total_orders                              as total_orders,
    m.delayed_orders                            as delayed_orders,
    m.delay_rate_pct                            as delay_rate_pct,
    m.avg_delivery_days                         as avg_delivery_days,
    m.avg_review_score                          as avg_review_score,
    m.total_spend                               as total_spend,
    m.first_order_at                            as first_order_at,
    m.last_order_at                             as last_order_at,
    dateDiff('day', m.first_order_at, m.last_order_at) as customer_lifetime_days,

    multiIf(
        m.total_orders >= 5, 'high_frequency',
        m.total_orders >= 2, 'repeat',
        'one_time'
    )                                           as customer_segment
from customer_metrics as m
left join customer_attributes as c on m.customer_id = c.customer_id
left join geolocation as g on c.customer_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix

order_delivered_carrier_date.name: order_delivered_carrier_date
order_delivered_carrier_date.description: Timestamp when the order was handed to the carrier.

order_delivered_customer_date.name: order_delivered_customer_date

order_month.description: First day of the purchase month, used for trend charts.

carrier_transit_days.name: carrier_transit_days

actual_delivery_days.name: actual_delivery_days
actual_delivery_days.description: End-to-end lead time in days from purchase to customer delivery.

delay_days.name: delay_days
delay_days.description: Signed difference between actual and estimated delivery, in days. Positive = late, negative = early, zero = exactly on time.

is_delayed.name: is_delayed
is_delayed.description: Binary SLA breach flag. 1 when delay_days > 0, otherwise 0.

price.name: price
price.description: Price of the first line item in BRL.

freight_value.name: freight_value
freight_value.description: Freight charged for the first line item in BRL.

total_order_value.name: total_order_value

product_weight_g.name: product_weight_g

customer_lat.name: customer_lat

customer_lng.name: customer_lng

        round(sum(total_order_value), 2)                    as total_revenue,
        min(order_purchase_timestamp)                       as first_order_at,

    coalesce(a.seller_state, 'unknown')         as seller_state,
    coalesce(a.seller_zip_code_prefix, '')      as seller_zip_code_prefix,

model.dustinadelixia_groceria.int_order_.raw_code:
{{ config(
    materialized='table',
    engine='MergeTree()',
    order_by='order_id'
) }}

/*
    Silver -> Gold bridge: one row per delivered order.

    Business grain: an order can contain several items and several sellers.
    To keep the fact table at order grain, the first item (lowest order_item_id)
    is used for the product and seller attributes, matching the original
    operational reporting definition.

    All SLA measures are derived here in SQL; no Python feature engineering.
*/

with orders as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_orders') }}

),

first_item as (

    select
        order_id,
        argMin(product_id, order_item_id)   as product_id,
        argMin(seller_id, order_item_id)    as seller_id,
        argMin(price, order_item_id)        as price,
        argMin(freight_value, order_item_id) as freight_value
    from {{ ref('stg_order_items') }}
    group by order_id

),

latest_review as (

    select
        order_id,
        argMax(review_score, review_answer_timestamp) as review_score
    from {{ ref('stg_order_reviews') }}
    group by order_id

),

customers as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_customers') }}

),

sellers as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_sellers') }}

),

products as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_products') }}

),

geolocation as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_geolocation') }}

),

enriched as (

    select
        o.order_id                                              as order_id,
        o.customer_id                                           as customer_id,
        o.order_status                                          as order_status,
        o.order_purchase_timestamp                              as order_purchase_timestamp,
        o.order_approved_at                                     as order_approved_at,
        o.order_delivered_carrier_date                          as order_delivered_carrier_date,
        o.order_delivered_customer_date                         as order_delivered_customer_date,
        o.order_estimated_delivery_date                         as order_estimated_delivery_date,

        coalesce(i.product_id, 'unknown')       as product_id,
        coalesce(p.product_category_name, 'unknown') as product_category_name,
        coalesce(p.product_weight_g, 0)         as product_weight_g,
        coalesce(i.price, 0)                    as price,
        coalesce(i.freight_value, 0)            as freight_value,

        coalesce(i.seller_id, 'unknown')        as seller_id,
        coalesce(s.seller_city, 'unknown')      as seller_city,
        coalesce(s.seller_state, 'unknown')     as seller_state,
        coalesce(s.seller_zip_code_prefix, '')  as seller_zip_code_prefix,

        c.customer_city                         as customer_city,
        c.customer_state                        as customer_state,

/*
    Silver: collapse many raw geolocation points to one coordinate per ZIP code
    prefix. Points outside the Brazilian bounding box are discarded to protect
    the regional map from bad GPS data.
*/

with source as (

    select *
    from {{ source('bronze', 'raw_geolocation') }}

),

valid_points as (

    select
        trim(toString(geolocation_zip_code_prefix))                     as geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
        geolocation_lat                                                 as lat,
        geolocation_lng                                                 as lng,
        coalesce(nullIf(lowerUTF8(trim(geolocation_city)), ''), 'unknown')  as city,
        coalesce(nullIf(upperUTF8(trim(geolocation_state)), ''), 'unknown') as state_code
    from source
    where
        notEmpty(trim(toString(geolocation_zip_code_prefix)))
        and geolocation_lat between -33.75 and 5.27
        and geolocation_lng between -73.99 and -34.79

)

select
    geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
    round(avg(lat), 6)          as lat,
    round(avg(lng), 6)          as lng,
    any(city)                   as city,
    any(state_code)             as state_code_code
from valid_points
group by geolocation_zip_code_prefix

        where snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key is null

        )

            source_data.*,
            snapshotted_data.dbt_scd_id

        from updates_source_data as source_data
        join snapshotted_data on snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key = source_data.dbt_unique_key
        where (
            {{ strategy.row_changed }}
        )
    )

    {%- if strategy.invalidate_hard_deletes -%}
    ,

    deletes as (

        select
            'delete' as dbt_change_type,
            source_data.*,
            {{ snapshot_get_time() }} as dbt_valid_from,
            {{ snapshot_get_time() }} as dbt_updated_at,

            snapshotted_data.dbt_scd_id

        where source_data.dbt_unique_key is null
    )
    {%- endif %}

    union all
    select * EXCEPT (ts) from updates
    {%- if strategy.invalidate_hard_deletes %}
    union all
    select * EXCEPT (ts) from deletes
    {%- endif %}

### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models
in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the
models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view
shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown
in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`
button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build,
or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.
